column2: I am building a small tool that keeps track of my university assignments. Right now it is a single Python script that reads a CSV file with columns for course, title, due date, weight, and status. Every morning it prints what is due in the next seven days, sorted by due date, and highlights anything worth more than ten percent of the final grade. It works, but it has problems. First, the CSV gets edited by hand and I often make typos in the date column, which crashes the script with a confusing error. Second, I want reminders on my phone, not just a printout in the terminal. Third, some courses post assignments on Canvas and I copy them over manually, which is tedious and I sometimes miss one. Fourth, I would like to see how much time I actually spent on each assignment compared to how long I expected it to take, so I can plan better. I have about ten hours a week to work on this over the next month. I know Python well, I have used Flask once, and I have a free Supabase account. I am comfortable with SQL but have never built a mobile app. I would rather not pay for anything. Given all of that, please propose a concrete plan. Break it into weekly milestones, say which parts to build first and why, suggest how to store the data, explain how to get reminders to my phone without writing a native app, and describe how to validate the dates so a typo gives a clear message instead of a crash. Also tell me which parts are risky or likely to take longer than I expect, and what I could cut if I run out of time. Finally, sketch the database tables with their columns and types, and give a short example of the validation code in Python.
